correctness.rationale: The frozen formula for a=2 is true, but its asserted resolution was already known. The replacement finding consists only of the finite obstruction for a>=3 and its fixed-a liminf. Re-audit of the replacement: gcd(a,Q_a(R))=1 gives a CRT class modulo m=aQ_a(R). Its first representative above Rb lies at most m beyond Rb and strictly below (R+1)b by m<b. Reduction of any nonnegative representation modulo a forces y congruent to -1 modulo a, so y>=a-1>=2 and is coprime to a; y<=R by the upper interval endpoint. If no such y exists, there is no representation. Otherwise any prime factor of y divides Q_a(R) and n but not a, and hence also divides x. The argument works if x=0 or if Q_a(R)=1. With fixed a, the omitted prime logarithms have bounded sum, so log Q_a(R)=R+o(R); taking floor((1-epsilon)log b) makes m<b for every sufficiently large coprime b, proving the liminf with constant one. The repair's two replay examples were checked, including the empty product. A separate seven-example nonnegative-solution enumeration corroborated the frozen finite obstruction; the uploaded verify.py was inspected rather than executed. Finite examples are not the proof.
residual_risks: No optimality of the lower constant or fixed-a upper asymptotic is demonstrated; the liminf is not asserted uniformly for growing a.

The surviving contribution is the explicit uniformly applicable finite witness in (Rb,(R+1)b) and its sharpening from a published subsequence lower bound to the all-coprime-b lower bound with leading liminf constant one. value.rationale: The exact finite obstruction can be replayed for any admissible b above a simple explicit threshold, and resolves a demonstrable gap left by the earlier subsequence bound. It establishes divergence of g(a,b)/b uniformly over large b at each fixed a>=3, in contrast to the known bounded a=2 behavior. This is a meaningful change in quantifier and order, not a new claim based on recomputing the prior exact boundary. Value is re-evaluated on the finite obstruction and all-b asymptotic only.
residual_risks: The finite parameter threshold is sufficient, not optimized; the theorem is a lower bound, not a classification of all exceptions.
